title: Exact Minimum Refresh-Gadget Count for Gimli
summary: A secure construction gives an upper bound of 120 gadgets and a multiple-of-6 constraint, but whether this bound is optimal remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For the Gimli implementation under the register-probing attack model, determine the exact minimum number of refresh gadgets required for security. The implementation consists of six consecutive identical subcircuits, and using 20 refresh gadgets per subcircuit gives a secure construction, hence an upper bound of 120 gadgets; the optimum is known to be a multiple of 6, but its optimality cannot be established without an exhaustive search.

scope.domain: Side-channel cryptanalysis of masked bitsliced implementations under register-probing attacks.
assumptions: Security is evaluated under the register-probing attack model.
parameters: Refresh-gadget count, the quantity to minimize
Six consecutive identical subcircuits, determining the multiple-of-6 constraint
Twenty refresh gadgets per subcircuit, yielding the secure construction
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine the exact minimum number of refresh gadgets required for security and establish whether the upper bound of 120 is optimal; the source indicates that this requires an exhaustive search.

citations.label: Tornado: Automatic Generation of Probing-Secure Masked Bitsliced Implementations

progress.summary: The source presents a secure construction with 20 refresh gadgets for each of six identical subcircuits, giving an upper bound of 120 and a multiple-of-6 constraint. It states that the current method cannot establish optimality without exhaustive search.
